content:
After a long period of developer and public beta testing, Apple is now rolling out macOS 26.6 to all compatible Mac users. Here's what's in this update.

macOS 26.6 is officially here

macOS 26.6 is now available, fixing over 150 security vulnerabilities, along with other bug fixes and performance improvements. These include an issue where some Intel-only apps incorrectly showed a deprecation notice, bugs related to HealthKit, and issues with HDR screenshots in Messages.

For users planning to upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate later this year, macOS 26.6 should begin the process of pre-indexing for the new Siri AI, new Siri app, and other features related to the new version of Apple Intelligence.

Apple has only confirmed that iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6 will undergo this process, but it appears the same approach will be taken on Mac. As users currently running the macOS 27 beta are aware, the indexing process can take several days, so starting early should help reduce waiting time after upgrading later.

The official version number of macOS 26.6 is 25G72, which differs from last week's release candidate (25G70).

Have you found anything new in macOS 26.6? Let us know in the comments.
